summary: Planar Al/InAs Josephson junction chains achieve superinductance with characteristic impedance $Z = 4.7$ to $5.2~	ext{k}\ \
motivation: High-impedance superconducting circuits like fluxonium require superinductors, but tunnel junctions face a conflict: small charging energy $E_C \ll E_J$ minimizes phase slips but reduces plasma frequency $\omega_p \sim \sqrt{E_C E_J}$, whereas hybrid superconductor-semiconductor junctions could potentially evade this constraint through high transparency despite $E_C > E_J$.
method: Arrays of 800 planar Al/InAs junctions with lengths $l_J = 400$ or $700$ nm were fabricated on epitaxial InAs 2D electron gas (mobility $1.5 \times 10^4~\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{Vs}$, density $9.76 \times 10^{11}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$), coupled capacitively to a coplanar waveguide, and characterized via microwave spectroscopy and two-tone cross-Kerr measurements at $23~\mathrm{mK}$.
result: Devices with $l_J = 700$ nm exhibit $Z > R_Q$ (4.7–5.2 kΩ vs 1.03 kΩ), linear mode dispersion to $12~\mathrm{GHz}$ with junction inductance $1.8$–$2.14~\mathrm{nH}$ per unit cell, negligible shunt capacitance, but internal quality factors decay as $Q_i \propto 1/f_r$, decreasing an order of magnitude from 1–10 GHz; fitted shunt resistance $R_J \approx 10$–$11~\mathrm{k}\Omega$ (700 nm) or $3~\mathrm{k}\Omega$ (400 nm) is attributed to diffusive-junction loss.
